transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, what brought me in is that people keep telling me I'm not listening to them. Like, my supervisor at the plant, or my wife... they'll be talking straight to my face, and a minute later I realize I only caught maybe half of what they said, and I have to ask them to repeat it. It's frustrating. Speaking of my supervisor, he's this guy who used to work at the Ford plant up in Michigan before they downsized, and he always talks about how cold it gets up there. I can't even imagine. I hate the cold. My brother moved to Minnesota a few years back, and he says you have to plug your car in at night so the engine block doesn't freeze. Can you believe that? Plugging a car in like a toaster. Anyway, yeah, my wife is getting really fed up with having to repeat herself all the time.
Do you have trouble understanding people mainly when there’s background noise, or even when it’s quiet and they’re speaking directly to you?

I don't really know, honestly. I haven't really noticed if it's just when it's loud. I mean, the plant is always noisy, right? We've got these huge stamping presses going all shift, so you gotta wear those little foam earplugs. You know the neon orange ones? I can't stand them, they always pop out of my left ear. I tried to get the safety guy, Gary, to order the earmuff kind, but he said they're on backorder. Gary's always saying stuff is on backorder. I swear the guy just doesn't want to do the paperwork. He's got this little office right off the floor with a window, and he just sits in there drinking diet soda all day. He collects those old vintage soda bottles too, has them lined up all over his desk. 

But anyway... yeah, even at home when the TV is off and it's dead quiet, I still catch myself missing what my wife is saying. So I guess the background noise doesn't really make a difference.
Do you also often lose things like keys, paperwork, or your phone?

Lose things? No, not really. I always keep my keys clipped right here on my belt loop. Got this heavy-duty carabiner for it. My buddy Dave actually brought it back for me from Colorado. He went out there to do some rock climbing... which, honestly, you couldn't pay me enough to do. Hanging off a cliff by a rope? No way. I get dizzy just getting up on the ladder to clean the gutters out. 

Actually, last fall I was up there clearing out all these wet leaves, and this huge fat squirrel jumps out of the oak tree right onto the shingles, scared the absolute crap out of me. I almost dropped my scraper right into my wife's prize rosebushes. She would've had my head if I broke those. She spends every Sunday out there with this special fertilizer... smells awful, like fish or something. She buys it in these big gallon jugs at the garden center. 

But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, losing stuff. Yeah, no, I usually know exactly where my phone and my keys are. That's not really a problem for me.
Did you have similar trouble paying attention or listening as a child, before age 12?

Yeah, I was pretty much exactly like this when I was a kid. Actually, it might have been worse. My teachers were always moving my desk around because I just couldn't stay in my seat. I'd be up wandering around, or I'd just blurt out the answers before they even finished asking the question. They hated that. And I was always getting into trouble for messing with other kids' work, you know, just reaching over and grabbing their pencils or whatever. This was all way before middle school. 

Speaking of middle school, I went to Lincoln Middle. They tore it down a few years ago to build a strip mall. Can you believe that? A whole school, just gone, and now it's a mattress store and a frozen yogurt place. I went in there once, the yogurt place I mean, and they charge by the ounce. You get this huge cup and just pile it high, and before you know it, you're paying like twelve bucks for a cup of ice cream. Total ripoff. My wife loves it though, she gets all those little gummy worms on top. I don't get the appeal of gummy worms. They get stuck in your teeth. I had a cavity filled last year and the dentist told me to lay off the chewy candy. Dr. Henderson, nice guy, always has golf on the TV in the waiting room. 

But yeah, anyway, school was always tough for me. I was just all over the place.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview is consistent with childhood-onset ADHD, predominantly inattentive/combined features, with clear lifelong symptoms beginning before age 12: distractibility, poor sustained attention, not listening when spoken to directly, blurting out answers, difficulty staying seated, and fidgeting/wandering. Symptoms are present in more than one setting (work and home) and cause interpersonal/occupational friction. No evidence was obtained for alternative explanations such as hearing loss, psychosis, mood episode, or substance-related causes.
